Fetch a file from its source or a mirror, verified by its SHA-256

Source: R/fetch_verified.R
fetchvrf.Rd

Downloads url to dest, trying the source first (with its Wayback Machine snapshot as the source's own fallback, as blfetch does) and then each mirror in turn, and keeps the first copy whose SHA-256 is sha256. A copy with another digest is never used: a changed or truncated file is a different file.

Usage

fetchvrf(
  url,
  dest,
  sha256 = NULL,
  mirrors = character(),
  tmout = 120L,
  arcs = "rmorie"
)

Arguments

url

The source URL (https).

dest

The file to write.

sha256

The expected SHA-256, 64 hexadecimal characters, or NULL.

mirrors

Further URLs that serve the same file, tried in order after the source.

tmout

Seconds allowed for each download (default 120).

arcs

Archives tried after the source, its Wayback snapshot and the mirrors: "rmorie" (archive.rmorie.com, by arcget) and folders written by arccap (read from their WARC files), in order. character() tries none.

Value

Invisibly, a list: source ("live", "wayback", "mirror", "rmorie" or "local"), url (the URL that served the kept copy), sha256, bytes, and tried (a data frame of every attempt: url, outcome).

Details

Some servers refuse the Internet Archive's crawler while serving everyone else (Statistics Canada does), so a Wayback snapshot of their files may not exist. The remedy is a capture made from elsewhere, published as a mirror and pinned by its digest. It can be an Internet Archive item, at https://archive.org/download/ followed by <item>/<file>; the data service; or an institutional repository. Because the digest is checked, a mirror does not have to be trusted: a copy that matches is the same bytes the analysis used, wherever it came from.

Without sha256 the first copy that downloads is kept and its digest is returned, to be pinned for the next run.

See also

blfetch, sha256file, wbsave.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# a Statistics Canada table the Wayback Machine cannot capture, with the archive.org copy
# made from elsewhere as a mirror
item <- "https://archive.org/download/rmorie-statcan-indigenous-tables-2026-10"
fetchvrf("https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/tbl/csv/41100063-eng.zip",
               file.path(tempdir(), "41100063-eng.zip"),
               mirrors = paste0(item, "/41100063-eng.zip"))
}
